column1: #mapping_set_title: HETO links to RHEO and OHEO types (primary) and HEO concepts (secondary)

#mapping_set_description: Two tiers. Primary rows (mapping_tier primary) are exactly the catalogue links HETO asserts in heto.ttl, from a task specification (an individual) to a RHEO, OHEO or IAO class, with the HETO predicate that says what the task does with it, which is involves type (heto:3000002), has input type (heto:3000003), has output type (heto:3000004) or has process type (heto:3000005). These are HETO's logical links, to real things as RHEO and OHEO define them. Secondary rows (mapping_tier secondary) are in this file only and are skos:relatedMatch. They are the task-to-concept rows to HEO, for learning and navigation only, which state no requirement, and the class-level mappings from a kind of task to a HEO concept or a RHEO or OHEO type, which are different kinds of thing. Before 0.2.0 the task-to-concept rows used requires concept (heto:3000001), now obsolete. No row states identity and none uses skos:exactMatch. HEO concepts take the prefix hewc, as in the other ontologies of the family. Entity types use the SSSOM 1.0 text values.

#comment: Written by src/build_heto.py and drafted by Michelle Ashley with Claude. Every row is proposed and unreviewed, so mapping_justification is semapv:UnspecifiedMatching. It becomes semapv:ManualMappingCuration, with reviewer_id and reviewer_label, when a named curator (Darrin Baines, orcid:0000-0001-9502-4678, or Michelle Ashley, orcid:0009-0006-0231-3731) signs a row off, and rejected rows are removed. Confidence is a house scale, 0.9 when the object is the task's own method, input or output as the task definition names it, 0.8 for a main input, output, process type or needed concept, and 0.7 for a related thing. Each reason states why the link holds and then quotes both definitions. The rows give no linking kind (HEAO_9000001) yet; that is planned for HETO 0.3.0.

The task is the carrying out of an economic evaluation, which the concept explains. HETO defines Conduct a model-based economic evaluation as "A task specification for comparing the costs and health outcomes of two or more options for a stated decision problem by means of an economic model, so that a decision maker can judge which option offers better value."; HEO defines Economic Evaluation as "Economic evaluation, often called health economic evaluation, compares the costs and outcomes of healthcare options to judge which offers the best value.".

Cost-effectiveness analysis is the usual form of comparison the evaluation reports. HETO defines Conduct a model-based economic evaluation as "A task specification for comparing the costs and health outcomes of two or more options for a stated decision problem by means of an economic model, so that a decision maker can judge which option offers better value."; HEO defines Cost-Effectiveness Analysis as "Cost-effectiveness analysis compares healthcare options by the extra cost of each extra unit of health gained, such as cost per life-year gained.".

The evaluation is model-based, so the practitioner needs the idea of a health economic model. HETO defines Conduct a model-based economic evaluation as "A task specification for comparing the costs and health outcomes of two or more options for a stated decision problem by means of an economic model, so that a decision maker can judge which option offers better value."; HEO defines Health Economic Model as "A health economic model, or decision model, is a mathematical framework combining evidence to estimate the costs and health outcomes of healthcare options.".

Evidence for the model is taken from evidence source documents such as trial reports and cost schedules. HETO defines Conduct a model-based economic evaluation as "A task specification for comparing the costs and health outcomes of two or more options for a stated decision problem by means of an economic model, so that a decision maker can judge which option offers better value."; RHEO defines evidence source document as "A document from which an economic evaluation estimate is taken, such as a trial report, a published study, a national cost schedule or a registry report.".

The evaluation's results are model results such as total costs, QALYs and ICERs. HETO defines Conduct a model-based economic evaluation as "A task specification for comparing the costs and health outcomes of two or more options for a stated decision problem by means of an economic model, so that a decision maker can judge which option offers better value."; RHEO defines model result as "A data entity produced by a model run, such as a total cost, total quality-adjusted life years or an incremental cost-effectiveness ratio, for a stated option or comparison.".

The evaluation ends in a written report, a document. HETO defines Conduct a model-based economic evaluation as "A task specification for comparing the costs and health outcomes of two or more options for a stated decision problem by means of an economic model, so that a decision maker can judge which option offers better value."; IAO defines document as "A collection of information content entities intended to be understood together as a whole".

Results are produced by running the model, so model runs are part of the work. HETO defines Conduct a model-based economic evaluation as "A task specification for comparing the costs and health outcomes of two or more options for a stated decision problem by means of an economic model, so that a decision maker can judge which option offers better value."; RHEO defines model run as "A planned process in which an economic model version is executed with a set of parameter assignments to produce results for a stated analysis, such as the base case or a scenario.".

The evaluation is carried out with an economic model, the information entity that represents the decision problem. HETO defines Conduct a model-based economic evaluation as "A task specification for comparing the costs and health outcomes of two or more options for a stated decision problem by means of an economic model, so that a decision maker can judge which option offers better value."; RHEO defines economic model as "An information content entity that represents a decision problem mathematically and combines evidence and assumptions to estimate the costs and outcomes of the options compared.".

The evaluation starts from a stated decision problem. HETO defines Conduct a model-based economic evaluation as "A task specification for comparing the costs and health outcomes of two or more options for a stated decision problem by means of an economic model, so that a decision maker can judge which option offers better value."; RHEO defines decision problem specification as "An information content entity that states the decision an economic evaluation is to inform: the population, the options compared, the outcomes, the perspective, the setting and the time horizon.".

Patient-level trial or routine data used in the evaluation are evidence datasets. HETO defines Conduct a model-based economic evaluation as "A task specification for comparing the costs and health outcomes of two or more options for a stated decision problem by means of an economic model, so that a decision maker can judge which option offers better value."; RHEO defines evidence dataset as "An information content entity that is a collection of patient-level or aggregate data from which an economic evaluation estimate is calculated, such as a trial dataset or an extract of routine data.".

The task produces a statement of the decision problem, the concept it is named after. HETO defines Define the decision problem as "A task specification for stating the decision an economic evaluation is to inform, including the population, the options compared, the outcomes, the perspective and the time horizon, before any analysis begins."; HEO defines Decision Problem as "A decision problem is the choice an economic evaluation or model must inform, stated as population, options compared, outcomes, costs and decision maker.".

Choosing the comparators is one of the main actions of the task. HETO defines Define the decision problem as "A task specification for stating the decision an economic evaluation is to inform, including the population, the options compared, the outcomes, the perspective and the time horizon, before any analysis begins."; HEO defines Comparator as "A comparator is the alternative, such as current practice or another treatment, against which a new health intervention is compared in economic evaluation.".

PICO is a common way to structure the population, intervention, comparator and outcome elements. HETO defines Define the decision problem as "A task specification for stating the decision an economic evaluation is to inform, including the population, the options compared, the outcomes, the perspective and the time horizon, before any analysis begins."; HEO defines PICO Framework as "A structured framework specifying the Population, Intervention, Comparator, and Outcome, used to formulate a well-defined clinical or research question.".

Where a decision maker issues a scope, framing the decision problem starts from that scoping stage. HETO defines Define the decision problem as "A task specification for stating the decision an economic evaluation is to inform, including the population, the options compared, the outcomes, the perspective and the time horizon, before any analysis begins."; HEO defines Scoping as "The initial assessment stage in which the specific boundaries, including technology, population, comparators, and outcomes, are formally defined.".

Stating the population the decision concerns is one of the main actions. HETO defines Define the decision problem as "A task specification for stating the decision an economic evaluation is to inform, including the population, the options compared, the outcomes, the perspective and the time horizon, before any analysis begins."; HEO defines Target Population as "The group identified as the intended recipients of a treatment or intervention, based on clinical, demographic, or policy criteria.".

Aligning the methods with the decision maker's guidance means checking them against its reference case, where it has one. HETO defines Define the decision problem as "A task specification for stating the decision an economic evaluation is to inform, including the population, the options compared, the outcomes, the perspective and the time horizon, before any analysis begins."; HEO defines Reference Case as "A reference case is the set of methods, such as perspective, outcome measure and discounting, that HTA bodies like NICE expect economic evaluations to use.".

A scope or a decision maker's methods guidance, where one is issued, is a document the task starts from. HETO defines Define the decision problem as "A task specification for stating the decision an economic evaluation is to inform, including the population, the options compared, the outcomes, the perspective and the time horizon, before any analysis begins."; IAO defines document as "A collection of information content entities intended to be understood together as a whole".

The output of the task is a decision problem specification as RHEO defines it. HETO defines Define the decision problem as "A task specification for stating the decision an economic evaluation is to inform, including the population, the options compared, the outcomes, the perspective and the time horizon, before any analysis begins."; RHEO defines decision problem specification as "An information content entity that states the decision an economic evaluation is to inform: the population, the options compared, the outcomes, the perspective, the setting and the time horizon.".

The options compared are described by intervention specifications. HETO defines Define the decision problem as "A task specification for stating the decision an economic evaluation is to inform, including the population, the options compared, the outcomes, the perspective and the time horizon, before any analysis begins."; RHEO defines intervention specification as "A plan specification describing a health care intervention or programme that is one of the options compared in an economic evaluation.".

The population the decision concerns is described by a population specification. HETO defines Define the decision problem as "A task specification for stating the decision an economic evaluation is to inform, including the population, the options compared, the outcomes, the perspective and the time horizon, before any analysis begins."; RHEO defines population specification as "An information content entity that states the criteria, such as condition, severity, age range and care setting, defining the persons to whom an estimate, a study or a decision applies.".

The task chooses the perspective, and the concept explains what that choice settles, whose costs and outcomes the evaluation counts. HETO defines Define the evaluation perspective as "A task specification for stating whose costs and health outcomes an economic evaluation counts, such as those falling on the health system or on society as a whole, so that resources and outcomes are included consistently."; HEO defines Perspective as "Perspective in health economic evaluation is the viewpoint, such as the health system, payer or society, that decides which costs and outcomes are counted.".

The societal perspective is one of the perspectives the practitioner may choose between. HETO defines Define the evaluation perspective as "A task specification for stating whose costs and health outcomes an economic evaluation counts, such as those falling on the health system or on society as a whole, so that resources and outcomes are included consistently."; HEO defines Societal Perspective as "The societal perspective is an economic evaluation viewpoint that counts all costs and outcomes, whoever bears them, including productivity and carer time.".

The healthcare perspective, counting only costs and outcomes falling on the payer or provider, is the other usual choice. HETO defines Define the evaluation perspective as "A task specification for stating whose costs and health outcomes an economic evaluation counts, such as those falling on the health system or on society as a whole, so that resources and outcomes are included consistently."; HEO defines Healthcare Perspective as "An analytic viewpoint including only costs and outcomes falling on the healthcare payer or provider, excluding broader costs such as productivity loss.".

A decision maker's reference case may set the perspective, so it is consulted first. HETO defines Define the evaluation perspective as "A task specification for stating whose costs and health outcomes an economic evaluation counts, such as those falling on the health system or on society as a whole, so that resources and outcomes are included consistently."; HEO defines Reference Case as "A reference case is the set of methods, such as perspective, outcome measure and discounting, that HTA bodies like NICE expect economic evaluations to use.".

The perspective is chosen for a stated decision problem. HETO defines Define the evaluation perspective as "A task specification for stating whose costs and health outcomes an economic evaluation counts, such as those falling on the health system or on society as a whole, so that resources and outcomes are included consistently."; RHEO defines decision problem specification as "An information content entity that states the decision an economic evaluation is to inform: the population, the options compared, the outcomes, the perspective, the setting and the time horizon.".

The output is a perspective specification, which lists the kinds of resource counted. HETO defines Define the evaluation perspective as "A task specification for stating whose costs and health outcomes an economic evaluation counts, such as those falling on the health system or on society as a whole, so that resources and outcomes are included consistently."; RHEO defines perspective specification as "A directive information entity stating whose resources and outcomes an economic evaluation counts, such as the health and personal social services system or society as a whole, by listing the kinds of resource included.".

The perspective is stated by listing the kinds of resource it includes, each identified by a resource type specification. HETO defines Define the evaluation perspective as "A task specification for stating whose costs and health outcomes an economic evaluation counts, such as those falling on the health system or on society as a whole, so that resources and outcomes are included consistently."; RHEO defines resource type specification as "A costed item type specification that identifies a kind of resource unit that is consumed, occupied or used in care, such as a hospital bed day, a 28-day pack of a medicine, a vaccine dose or an hour of staff or carer time, optionally with a code from a classification.".

The task chooses the time horizon and records the reason, and the concept explains what the horizon has to cover. HETO defines Set the time horizon as "A task specification for choosing the period over which an economic evaluation counts costs and health outcomes, long enough to capture the differences between the options compared."; HEO defines Time Horizon as "The span of time over which an economic evaluation captures relevant differences in costs and outcomes among the options being compared.".

The horizon is chosen for a stated decision problem. HETO defines Set the time horizon as "A task specification for choosing the period over which an economic evaluation counts costs and health outcomes, long enough to capture the differences between the options compared."; RHEO defines decision problem specification as "An information content entity that states the decision an economic evaluation is to inform: the population, the options compared, the outcomes, the perspective, the setting and the time horizon.".

RHEO records the time horizon on the decision problem specification (has time horizon), so the updated specification is the output. HETO defines Set the time horizon as "A task specification for choosing the period over which an economic evaluation counts costs and health outcomes, long enough to capture the differences between the options compared."; RHEO defines decision problem specification as "An information content entity that states the decision an economic evaluation is to inform: the population, the options compared, the outcomes, the perspective, the setting and the time horizon.".

The task builds a health economic model, the concept that explains what is built. HETO defines Develop an economic model as "A task specification for building an economic model that represents a stated decision problem and combines evidence and assumptions to estimate the costs and health outcomes of the options compared."; HEO defines Health Economic Model as "A health economic model, or decision model, is a mathematical framework combining evidence to estimate the costs and health outcomes of healthcare options.".

Populating the model means estimating its parameters from evidence. HETO defines Develop an economic model as "A task specification for building an economic model that represents a stated decision problem and combines evidence and assumptions to estimate the costs and health outcomes of the options compared."; HEO defines Parameter Estimation as "Parameter estimation is the process of using evidence and a specified model or estimating rule to infer the values of quantities needed to describe a population, relationship, or decision model.".

A model is built to address a stated decision problem. HETO defines Develop an economic model as "A task specification for building an economic model that represents a stated decision problem and combines evidence and assumptions to estimate the costs and health outcomes of the options compared."; RHEO defines decision problem specification as "An information content entity that states the decision an economic evaluation is to inform: the population, the options compared, the outcomes, the perspective, the setting and the time horizon.".

Parameter values are taken from evidence source documents. HETO defines Develop an economic model as "A task specification for building an economic model that represents a stated decision problem and combines evidence and assumptions to estimate the costs and health outcomes of the options compared."; RHEO defines evidence source document as "A document from which an economic evaluation estimate is taken, such as a trial report, a published study, a national cost schedule or a registry report.".

The output is a fixed, identified economic model version that can be run. HETO defines Develop an economic model as "A task specification for building an economic model that represents a stated decision problem and combines evidence and assumptions to estimate the costs and health outcomes of the options compared."; RHEO defines economic model version as "An information content entity that is a fixed, identified state of an economic model, with a defined structure and set of parameters, that can be run to produce results.".

Building the model defines its named input quantities, the model parameters. HETO defines Develop an economic model as "A task specification for building an economic model that represents a stated decision problem and combines evidence and assumptions to estimate the costs and health outcomes of the options compared."; RHEO defines model parameter as "An information content entity that is a named input quantity of an economic model version, such as the utility of a health state or a transition probability.".

The work produces an economic model, of which each version is a fixed state. HETO defines Develop an economic model as "A task specification for building an economic model that represents a stated decision problem and combines evidence and assumptions to estimate the costs and health outcomes of the options compared."; RHEO defines economic model as "An information content entity that represents a decision problem mathematically and combines evidence and assumptions to estimate the costs and outcomes of the options compared.".

Each parameter is given its value by a parameter assignment that records the reason for the choice. HETO defines Develop an economic model as "A task specification for building an economic model that represents a stated decision problem and combines evidence and assumptions to estimate the costs and health outcomes of the options compared."; RHEO defines parameter assignment as "An information content entity recording that, in a stated economic model version, a stated model parameter takes the value of one stated economic evaluation estimate or one stated modelling assumption, with the reason for the choice.".

Resource use estimates are among the values the model's parameters take. HETO defines Develop an economic model as "A task specification for building an economic model that represents a stated decision problem and combines evidence and assumptions to estimate the costs and health outcomes of the options compared."; RHEO defines resource use estimate as "An economic evaluation estimate of the quantity of a resource or a health care process used per person or per event over a stated period, in natural units.".

Unit cost estimates are taken in where the model values resource use itself. HETO defines Develop an economic model as "A task specification for building an economic model that represents a stated decision problem and combines evidence and assumptions to estimate the costs and health outcomes of the options compared."; RHEO defines unit cost estimate as "A cost estimate for one unit of a resource or of a health care process, such as one hospital bed day or one consultation.".

Cost estimates for options or states are taken in as model parameters. HETO defines Develop an economic model as "A task specification for building an economic model that represents a stated decision problem and combines evidence and assumptions to estimate the costs and health outcomes of the options compared."; RHEO defines cost estimate as "An economic evaluation estimate of the monetary value of resources consumed, valued from a stated perspective, in a stated currency and price year.".

Utility estimates give the quality weights of the model states. HETO defines Develop an economic model as "A task specification for building an economic model that represents a stated decision problem and combines evidence and assumptions to estimate the costs and health outcomes of the options compared."; RHEO defines utility estimate as "An economic evaluation estimate of the preference-based value of a health state on a scale on which full health is 1 and dead is 0, obtained by a stated valuation method and, for indirect methods, a stated instrument and value set.".

Probability estimates give the chances of moving between model states. HETO defines Develop an economic model as "A task specification for building an economic model that represents a stated decision problem and combines evidence and assumptions to estimate the costs and health outcomes of the options compared."; RHEO defines probability estimate as "An economic evaluation estimate of the probability that a kind of clinical event occurs, either within a stated time interval or per event, in a stated population.".

Relative effect estimates give the effect of each option on the model's transitions. HETO defines Develop an economic model as "A task specification for building an economic model that represents a stated decision problem and combines evidence and assumptions to estimate the costs and health outcomes of the options compared."; RHEO defines relative effect estimate as "An economic evaluation estimate of the effect of an intervention relative to a comparator, expressed as a ratio or a difference, such as a hazard ratio or a relative risk.".

Assumptions adopted where no estimate exists are produced and recorded while the model is built. HETO defines Develop an economic model as "A task specification for building an economic model that represents a stated decision problem and combines evidence and assumptions to estimate the costs and health outcomes of the options compared."; RHEO defines modelling assumption as "An information content entity that states a value or a condition adopted in an analysis without direct estimation from data, together with its justification.".

The task is the conceptualisation stage the concept describes. HETO defines Conceptualise the model structure as "A task specification for deciding how an economic model will represent the decision problem, including the modelling technique, the health states or events, the pathways between them and the main assumptions, before the model is built."; HEO defines Model Conceptualization as "The initial stage of model development in which the disease process and decision problem are structured into a framework before technical build.".

The result of the task is a model structure. HETO defines Conceptualise the model structure as "A task specification for deciding how an economic model will represent the decision problem, including the modelling technique, the health states or events, the pathways between them and the main assumptions, before the model is built."; HEO defines Model Structure as "The overall organisation of a health economic model, including its technique, the health states or events represented, and how they link together.".

Choices made here are the source of structural uncertainty examined later. HETO defines Conceptualise the model structure as "A task specification for deciding how an economic model will represent the decision problem, including the modelling technique, the health states or events, the pathways between them and the main assumptions, before the model is built."; HEO defines Structural Uncertainty as "Structural uncertainty is doubt about how a health economic model represents a decision problem, such as its health states, pathways or extrapolation.".

Choosing the modelling technique often means choosing a state-transition model, the general class of Markov-type models. HETO defines Conceptualise the model structure as "A task specification for deciding how an economic model will represent the decision problem, including the modelling technique, the health states or events, the pathways between them and the main assumptions, before the model is built."; HEO defines State Transition Model as "A general term for a decision-analytic model, such as a Markov model, representing disease progression as movement between defined health states.".

A decision tree is the other common technique, for short-term or one-off decisions. HETO defines Conceptualise the model structure as "A task specification for deciding how an economic model will represent the decision problem, including the modelling technique, the health states or events, the pathways between them and the main assumptions, before the model is built."; HEO defines Decision Tree as "A decision tree is a branching model used in economic evaluation: strategies, chance events and end points give each option's expected costs and QALYs.".

The structure is designed to represent a stated decision problem. HETO defines Conceptualise the model structure as "A task specification for deciding how an economic model will represent the decision problem, including the modelling technique, the health states or events, the pathways between them and the main assumptions, before the model is built."; RHEO defines decision problem specification as "An information content entity that states the decision an economic evaluation is to inform: the population, the options compared, the outcomes, the perspective, the setting and the time horizon.".

The structure names the model states the model will use. HETO defines Conceptualise the model structure as "A task specification for deciding how an economic model will represent the decision problem, including the modelling technique, the health states or events, the pathways between them and the main assumptions, before the model is built."; RHEO defines model state as "A health state description used as a state of an economic model, such as stable disease or progressed disease in a cohort model, that stands for the clinical or classification state descriptions it approximates.".

The structure states which transitions between states are allowed. HETO defines Conceptualise the model structure as "A task specification for deciding how an economic model will represent the decision problem, including the modelling technique, the health states or events, the pathways between them and the main assumptions, before the model is built."; RHEO defines transition specification as "A directive information entity, part of an economic model version or adopted for recording under a classification scheme version, stating which transitions between states are allowed, such as that no transition leaves the state dead, or that treatment cannot restart after it has stopped.".

Structural assumptions are recorded with their justification as modelling assumptions. HETO defines Conceptualise the model structure as "A task specification for deciding how an economic model will represent the decision problem, including the modelling technique, the health states or events, the pathways between them and the main assumptions, before the model is built."; RHEO defines modelling assumption as "An information content entity that states a value or a condition adopted in an analysis without direct estimation from data, together with its justification.".

The structure draws on clinical evidence and published models, held in evidence source documents. HETO defines Conceptualise the model structure as "A task specification for deciding how an economic model will represent the decision problem, including the modelling technique, the health states or events, the pathways between them and the main assumptions, before the model is built."; RHEO defines evidence source document as "A document from which an economic evaluation estimate is taken, such as a trial report, a published study, a national cost schedule or a registry report.".

The task estimates resource use, the quantities the concept describes. HETO defines Estimate resource use as "A task specification for identifying and measuring the quantities of resources, such as staff time, medicines and hospital stays, used with each option or in each modelled health state, in natural units."; HEO defines Resource Use as "The physical quantities of inputs, such as staff time, equipment, and supplies, consumed in delivering a healthcare intervention.".

The concept is the counting of resources before they are valued, which is this task. HETO defines Estimate resource use as "A task specification for identifying and measuring the quantities of resources, such as staff time, medicines and hospital stays, used with each option or in each modelled health state, in natural units."; HEO defines Cost Measurement as "Cost measurement is the step in economic evaluation that counts the resources each alternative uses, such as GP visits or bed-days, before they are valued.".

Deciding which kinds of resource are relevant is the first action of the task. HETO defines Estimate resource use as "A task specification for identifying and measuring the quantities of resources, such as staff time, medicines and hospital stays, used with each option or in each modelled health state, in natural units."; HEO defines Resource Identification as "The process of determining which categories of resource use, such as staff time and supplies, are relevant when costing an intervention.".

The perspective specification lists the kinds of resource to be counted. HETO defines Estimate resource use as "A task specification for identifying and measuring the quantities of resources, such as staff time, medicines and hospital stays, used with each option or in each modelled health state, in natural units."; RHEO defines perspective specification as "A directive information entity stating whose resources and outcomes an economic evaluation counts, such as the health and personal social services system or society as a whole, by listing the kinds of resource included.".

Resource use records are one source of the quantities measured. HETO defines Estimate resource use as "A task specification for identifying and measuring the quantities of resources, such as staff time, medicines and hospital stays, used with each option or in each modelled health state, in natural units."; RHEO defines resource use record as "A measurement datum recording the quantity of a kind of resource used in a stated health care, social care or informal care process, in stated units.".

Published studies and trial reports are another source of quantities. HETO defines Estimate resource use as "A task specification for identifying and measuring the quantities of resources, such as staff time, medicines and hospital stays, used with each option or in each modelled health state, in natural units."; RHEO defines evidence source document as "A document from which an economic evaluation estimate is taken, such as a trial report, a published study, a national cost schedule or a registry report.".

The output is a resource use estimate in natural units, per person or per event. HETO defines Estimate resource use as "A task specification for identifying and measuring the quantities of resources, such as staff time, medicines and hospital stays, used with each option or in each modelled health state, in natural units."; RHEO defines resource use estimate as "An economic evaluation estimate of the quantity of a resource or a health care process used per person or per event over a stated period, in natural units.".

Each estimate concerns a kind of resource unit, identified by a resource type specification. HETO defines Estimate resource use as "A task specification for identifying and measuring the quantities of resources, such as staff time, medicines and hospital stays, used with each option or in each modelled health state, in natural units."; RHEO defines resource type specification as "A costed item type specification that identifies a kind of resource unit that is consumed, occupied or used in care, such as a hospital bed day, a 28-day pack of a medicine, a vaccine dose or an hour of staff or carer time, optionally with a code from a classification.".

Resource use is often estimated for each model state, as RHEO's state maintenance resource use expects. HETO defines Estimate resource use as "A task specification for identifying and measuring the quantities of resources, such as staff time, medicines and hospital stays, used with each option or in each modelled health state, in natural units."; RHEO defines model state as "A health state description used as a state of an economic model, such as stable disease or progressed disease in a cohort model, that stands for the clinical or classification state descriptions it approximates.".

Trial or routine patient-level data on resource use are evidence datasets. HETO defines Estimate resource use as "A task specification for identifying and measuring the quantities of resources, such as staff time, medicines and hospital stays, used with each option or in each modelled health state, in natural units."; RHEO defines evidence dataset as "An information content entity that is a collection of patient-level or aggregate data from which an economic evaluation estimate is calculated, such as a trial dataset or an extract of routine data.".

The task attaches a unit cost to each kind of resource counted, and the concept explains what a unit cost is. HETO defines Select unit costs as "A task specification for choosing the cost of one unit of each resource used in an economic evaluation, from sources that fit the perspective, the setting and the price year of the analysis."; HEO defines Unit Cost as "The cost of producing or delivering a single unit of a good or service, such as the cost per hospital bed-day.".

Unit costs are the values used to turn measured resource use into costs. HETO defines Select unit costs as "A task specification for choosing the cost of one unit of each resource used in an economic evaluation, from sources that fit the perspective, the setting and the price year of the analysis."; HEO defines Cost Valuation as "Cost valuation is the assignment of monetary values to measured resource use in accordance with a specified perspective, setting, price year, and decision purpose.".

Unit costs from other years are adjusted to the analysis price year. HETO defines Select unit costs as "A task specification for choosing the cost of one unit of each resource used in an economic evaluation, from sources that fit the perspective, the setting and the price year of the analysis."; HEO defines Inflation Adjustment as "The process of restating cost data from different time periods in constant, comparable price terms, typically using a relevant price index.".

When no published unit cost fits, the unit cost is built up from its resource components by micro-costing. HETO defines Select unit costs as "A task specification for choosing the cost of one unit of each resource used in an economic evaluation, from sources that fit the perspective, the setting and the price year of the analysis."; HEO defines Micro-Costing as "Micro-costing is a detailed method of estimating the cost of healthcare activities by identifying and measuring their individual resource components and valuing each component with an appropriate unit cost.".

A unit cost is chosen for each kind of resource unit counted. HETO defines Select unit costs as "A task specification for choosing the cost of one unit of each resource used in an economic evaluation, from sources that fit the perspective, the setting and the price year of the analysis."; RHEO defines resource type specification as "A costed item type specification that identifies a kind of resource unit that is consumed, occupied or used in care, such as a hospital bed day, a 28-day pack of a medicine, a vaccine dose or an hour of staff or carer time, optionally with a code from a classification.".

Unit costs are taken from evidence source documents such as national cost schedules. column7: related HEO concept (class level, learning and navigation)
column23: The HETO class classifies specifications of work whose result is a statement of the decision problem; the HEO concept explains what a decision problem is. column7: related HEO concept (class level, learning and navigation)
column23: The HETO class classifies specifications of the work of building a model; the HEO concept explains the model itself. column7: related RHEO or OHEO type (class level, in this file only)
column23: The RHEO class is the economic model as information; the HETO class is the specification of work whose result is such a model or part of one. column7: related HEO concept (class level, learning and navigation)
column23: Counting resources is one of the kinds of work the HETO class classifies; the HEO concept explains that step. HETO defines costing task specification as "A task specification whose intended result is the identification, measurement or valuation of the resources used by the options compared in an economic evaluation."; HEO defines Cost Measurement as "Cost measurement is the step in economic evaluation that counts the resources each alternative uses, such as GP visits or bed-days, before they are valued.".

column7: related HEO concept (class level, learning and navigation)
column23: Valuing measured resource use is another kind of work the HETO class classifies; the HEO concept explains that step. HETO defines costing task specification as "A task specification whose intended result is the identification, measurement or valuation of the resources used by the options compared in an economic evaluation."; HEO defines Cost Valuation as "Cost valuation is the assignment of monetary values to measured resource use in accordance with a specified perspective, setting, price year, and decision purpose.".

column7: related RHEO or OHEO type (class level, in this file only)
column23: The RHEO class is the process in which money values are attached to resource use; the HETO class is the specification of costing work, a different kind of thing. HETO defines costing task specification as "A task specification whose intended result is the identification, measurement or valuation of the resources used by the options compared in an economic evaluation."; RHEO defines costing process as "A planned process in which a monetary value is attached to recorded resource use, to care processes, to absences from work or to other cost records, from a stated perspective, producing cost records.".

column7: related HEO concept (class level, learning and navigation)
column23: The HETO class classifies specifications of work that place values on health states; the HEO concept explains health state valuation. column7: related RHEO or OHEO type (class level, in this file only)
column23: The OHEO class is the process of eliciting values for health states; HETO's outcome valuation tasks often choose among the results of such processes rather than carry one out. HETO defines health outcome valuation task specification as "A task specification whose intended result is a value placed on health outcomes or health states, such as the utility values given to the states of an economic model."; OHEO defines health state valuation process as "A preference elicitation process that obtains values or orderings for health states, from which utilities on a scale on which full health is 1 and dead is 0 are taken directly or estimated by modelling.".

column7: related HEO concept (class level, learning and navigation)
column23: The HETO class classifies specifications of uncertainty analysis work; the HEO concept explains sensitivity analysis, the main method used. HETO defines uncertainty analysis task specification as "A task specification whose intended result is a description of how uncertainty in inputs, assumptions or model structure affects the results or the decision of an economic evaluation."; HEO defines Sensitivity Analysis as "Sensitivity analysis tests whether a health economic model's results and decision change when uncertain inputs, assumptions or model structure are varied.".

column7: related HEO concept (class level, learning and navigation)
column23: The HETO class classifies specifications of validation work; the HEO concept explains model validation. column7: related HEO concept (class level, learning and navigation)
column23: The HETO class classifies specifications of work that compare options; the HEO concept explains the incremental comparison of several options.
